title: I’m developing FrogSlap, an Android arcade game — here’s my Halloween update trailer
author: Remedion
selftext:
Hey everyone! I’m the developer behind **FrogSlap**, an Android arcade game about quick reactions and slapping frogs.

Frogs appear on lily pads, and you need to react quickly while dealing with different enemy types. As you progress, you explore different worlds, battle bosses, collect rewards, and combine powers and runes to improve your runs.

This trailer shows the Halloween event: **30 haunted levels, candy thieves, ghosts, and three boss encounters.**

I use **AI-assisted artwork and sprite sheets for the character animations**. One of the biggest challenges has been keeping the frogs consistent across individual animation frames, gameplay assets, and promotional images.

I work from existing character references and check proportions, colours, outlines, and shading. An individual image can look good on its own but still need corrections to fit the game. For sprite sheets, the poses also need to form a readable sequence without the character’s appearance changing between frames.

The animations need to remain clear at the small size the frogs appear on a phone screen, so consistency and readable movement matter as much as individual frame quality.

I’d love to hear from other developers:

* How do you maintain character consistency across AI-assisted sprite sheets?
* How do you check and correct animation frames?
* Does the trailer make the gameplay easy to understand?

**FrogSlap on Google Play:**  
[https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.remediongames.frogslap](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.remediongames.frogslap)

Thanks for taking a look!
